guard: `cotal up` renders server.conf from the whole validated tenant inventory, and refuses to render while any account record is unreadable
why: The eviction this suite guards is silent by construction: with the sibling dropped from
`resolver_preload` the broker still starts, the booted space still works, and nothing prints.
So a suite that only booted a two-tenant root and looked healthy would stay green through the
whole defect, and the cells that must notice are the ones that read the OTHER tenant.
Every command builds first and every restore rebuilds. `bin/cotal.ts` reaches the CLI through
`@cotal-ai/cli`, which resolves to `dist/`, so a mutation of `src` that skips the build is a
run of unmutated code wearing a mutant's verdict. Measured here: the render mutation graded
UNGRADABLE with no build in the command, and KILLED with one.

mutations.name: the render goes back to the one space being booted
mutations.expectRed: server.conf preloads the SIBLING tenant's account
mutations.cell: server.conf preloads the SIBLING tenant's account (not evicted by a boot that never named it)

mutations.name: an unreadable account record is skipped instead of refusing the render
mutations.expectRed: and left the previous config untouched
mutations.cell: …and left the previous config untouched (no partially-rendered tenant list)
mutations.note: Aimed where the guard actually lives, after measuring. The non-zero exit and the message naming the record belong to an OLDER guard: `resolveMeshTarget` (mesh-target.ts:182) refuses an uncertain tenant list on the target-resolution path `up` runs before it ever renders, so both of those cells stay green with this refusal removed. What `preloadSpaceAccounts` owns is that the config is not rewritten on the way to that refusal, and that is the cell this reddens.
